I have farmed this same 3 mu for fifty years. My back is not what it was, and two of my children work in the town now, so they send a little money home. I do not change much from year to year — what worked last year should work this year.

For wheat, I plant in October. I buy improved seed from the dealer in town, same kind my neighbor Old Wang uses — he got about 450 jin per mu last year. I use about 30 jin of diammonium phosphate per mu as base fertilizer when I plough, and then 30 jin of urea when the wheat turns green in spring. That gives me maybe 22 jin of nitrogen per mu. Some say it is too much but I would rather put a little extra than see yellow wheat. My well water is close by so I water four times — before winter, returning green, jointing, and when the grain is filling. Spray once for aphids if I see them, sometimes twice if the weather is warm and sticky.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. Hybrid seed only — the old kinds don't give enough. I put compound fertilizer in the row when seeding, then urea at the big trumpet stage. About 18 jin nitrogen per mu. Two waterings usually enough because summer rain helps. Spray once for corn borer.

I use rotary tiller — the tractor man comes through the village, costs less than ploughing deep. My 3 mu is small, every bag of fertilizer matters, but I will not cut too much or I lose grain.
